script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'more-towns',
  description: 'Add Belgrade, Anaconda and Sidney to the site, rebuild the base map, verify in tests and a browser',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Build towns', detail: 'towns.json, min_zoom rule, base map rebuild, docs', model: WORKER },
    { title: 'Verify towns', detail: 'tests, sample and live builds, browser check, fixes', model: WORKER },
  ],
}

const WT = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/wt-towns'
const COMMON = `You work in a git WORKTREE at ${WT} on branch claude/more-towns (from main). Every command runs there (cd ${WT} first; use absolute paths under ${WT} for every file you read or edit). Never touch /home/user/RoofingApp itself (another job is editing it). Never commit, never push, never change git state (git status/diff/log are fine). Never write a model, vendor or AI-product name into any repo file. Plain wording, sentence case, no em-dashes in new prose. Verify first: git -C ${WT} branch --show-current must print claude/more-towns.

TASK (owner Carson, 2026-10-17): add every Montana city with a 2020 census population above 8,000 that the site lacks, plus Sidney at his request. Today's 14 towns: Billings, Bozeman, Butte, Glasgow, Glendive, Great Falls, Havre, Helena, Kalispell, Lewistown, Livingston, Miles City, Missoula, West Yellowstone. Add exactly three (2020 census, Wikipedia list of municipalities; coordinates from each town's infobox):
- Belgrade, Gallatin County, 10,460, lat 45.7803 lon -111.1752 (12 km west of Bozeman: its bubble would cover Bozeman's below about zoom 9)
- Anaconda (Anaconda-Deer Lodge County, consolidated), 9,421, lat 46.133 lon -112.933 (35 km west of Butte: bubbles touch below about zoom 8)
- Sidney, Richland County, 6,346, lat 47.7155 lon -104.1672 (north-east corner; Glendive is 65 km south and is a minor town)
Whitefish (7,751) and Laurel (7,222) are under 8,000: do not add them. Census-designated places (Lockwood, Evergreen) are not towns: do not add them.

RULES OF THE SITE you must honour: website/towns.json is the town list (AGENTS.md: set a new town's label side there; the label test must pass); the base map is rebuilt by python tools/build_basemap.py (downloads Natural Earth and us-atlas, pinned by hash; keep the downloads with --src ${WT}/../basemap-src so a rerun is fast) and committed; tests/test_basemap.py fails until it is rebuilt. "minor": true today means a town shows from zoom 7 (tools/build_basemap.py lines 841, 885-889, 1115, 1234, 1499; website/static/map/map.js lines 401, 632, 1354-1356, 1786; tools/smoke_map.py line 79; docs/DESIGN.md line 150). Generalise it to an integer "min_zoom" per town (default 5; "minor": true keeps meaning 7, so the four minor towns need no change): Belgrade min_zoom 9, Anaconda 8 (check both in the browser and raise or lower by one if bubbles still overlap or names collide; the label test is the arbiter for names). Python decides the rule (build.py's map_data passes "min_zoom" to data/map.json next to "minor"); map.js reads t.min_zoom (fallback: minor 7, else 5) in its four places, each change commented in the file's own style. The sample data (website/sample.py) must serve the new towns too (check the dict lookups by slug have defaults; invent SAMPLE values only where a dict needs an entry for a sensible page). Docs: README.md line 109 ("the 14 towns"), docs/DESIGN.md line 150 (the minor-town sentence becomes the min_zoom rule, naming the two new towns' zooms), docs/ROADMAP.md line 115 (the open question: answered 2026-10-17, state what was added and why), docs/DECISIONS.md: a new entry D31 "Towns: every Montana city over 8,000 plus Sidney (2026-10-17)" in the house style (bold title line, a short paragraph with the census figures and the min_zoom rule, then "*Why:*"). NWS offices: the build looks them up live; expected Belgrade -> Great Falls, Anaconda -> Missoula, Sidney -> Glasgow.`

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    files_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    tests: { type: 'string' },
    failures: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    open_issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['files_changed', 'tests', 'failures', 'open_issues', 'notes'],
}

phase('Build towns')
const build = await agent(`${COMMON}

STAGE 1, build. Do it in this order: (1) read towns.json, build_basemap.py's town handling, map.js's four minor places, build.py map_data, sample.py, tests/test_basemap.py and tests/test_site.py; (2) edit towns.json; (3) implement min_zoom in build_basemap.py, build.py and map.js, and in tools/smoke_map.py line 79 (count towns whose min_zoom is below 7 as the ones shown at the first view); (4) rebuild the base map: python tools/build_basemap.py --src ${WT}/../basemap-src (then --check must exit 0); (5) run python -m unittest discover -s tests (all must pass) and the sample builds python -m website.build --out ${WT}/../towns-off --sample and with --storm-layers; (6) docs. Report measured facts (basemap.json bytes before and after, label changes the builder printed, which label sides you chose and why).`, { label: 'build:towns', phase: 'Build towns', model: WORKER, schema: SCHEMA })
log('Build towns: ' + (build ? build.failures.length + ' failures, ' + build.open_issues.length + ' open issues' : 'no result'))

phase('Verify towns')
const verify = await agent(`${COMMON}

STAGE 2, verify and fix. The builder's report: ${JSON.stringify(build)}.
Do, and record each result: (1) git -C ${WT} diff --stat and read every changed file end to end; check the three coordinates against the task, and that nothing else in towns.json changed; (2) python -m unittest discover -s tests must pass; python tools/build_basemap.py --src ${WT}/../basemap-src --check must exit 0; (3) sample builds (both flags) and the browser smoke: PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium python tools/smoke_map.py <sample dir> and python tools/smoke_pages.py <sample dir> must pass; (4) a live build: python -m website.build --out ${WT}/../towns-live --require-live and read its status table and content: Belgrade, Anaconda and Sidney must have an NWS forecast, an office (Great Falls, Missoula, Glasgow) and station readings like the other towns; (5) in Chromium (Playwright, a scratch script outside the repo) open the live build's map.html at 1280x800 and 390x844, then zoom and pan to Bozeman at zooms 7, 8, 9 and to Butte at zooms 7, 8, and to Sidney at zoom 5 and 7: take screenshots into ${WT}/../towns-shots/ and LOOK at them (Read the PNGs): no bubble may cover another bubble or a name, Belgrade must appear only from its min_zoom, Anaconda from its; if anything overlaps, adjust min_zoom or the label side, rebuild the base map and re-run the tests; (6) the Now page lists 17 town cards and each new town page opens; (7) git diff of website/static/map/basemap.json: describe what changed (new places, shifted min_zooms) and confirm the file is still under its size budget test. Fix real defects minimally; never weaken a test. Report every command and result, and anything you could not verify.`, { label: 'verify:towns', phase: 'Verify towns', model: WORKER, schema: SCHEMA })

return { build, verify }

build.tests: python -m unittest discover -s tests: 281 tests OK (277 before the change, plus 4 new). tools/build_basemap.py --src .../scratchpad/basemap-src --check: exit 0 (committed file up to date). Sample builds with and without --storm-layers both built; tools/smoke_map.py passed on both (Playwright, /opt/pw-browsers chromium-1248). tools/smoke_pages.py passed at 288, 320, 375, 768 and 1440 px, light and dark. desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload: PASS (payload untouched). Nothing committed or pushed; git status shows 14 modified files.
failures: Fixed during the run, none failing at the end: tools/smoke_map.py timed out in four helper checks because the first town in towns.json (Anaconda) is hidden at the first view; those waits now use state="attached".

Fixed during the run: test_site.py station-ID literals (SMP100/SMP091) and test_basemap.py's zoom-5 contact count (2) broke when the towns were inserted; station IDs are now derived from site.TOWNS and the count is 3 (Miles City's name into Sidney's bubble).

Fixed during the run: the first layout check (Sidney label left, Glasgow label right) reported Glasgow's name into Sidney's bubble at zoom 5 (5.1 px, beyond the 4 px allowance). Fixed by Glasgow's label on top and Sidney's on top.
open_issues: Phone first view (390x844 and 360x740 open at zoom 5.25): Glasgow's name (top) sits 1.0 px from Havre's name (right) in Chromium. They do not overlap. Glasgow's other label sides collide at zoom 5 (right: Sidney's bubble, 5.1 px; left: Havre's bubble, 9.4 px; bottom: the Great Falls and Miles City names). Hiding Sidney below zoom 6 would remove the near-touch; the owner should choose.

Zoom 5.0 only (a very narrow phone): Miles City's name reaches 3.5 px into Sidney's bubble in Chromium, rings included. Inside the 4 px zoom-5 allowance, but new. Missoula's name into Kalispell's bubble measures 4.5 px with rings (the model says 3.5 px); that is unchanged from the committed build.

The brief's distances do not match the coordinates. Belgrade is 15.4 km north-west of Bozeman (bearing 318 degrees), not 12 km west. Glendive is 79 km south-south-west of Sidney, not 65 km south. Anaconda is 33.9 km west-north-west of Butte (the brief's 35 km is close).

Anaconda's zoom is 8 (brief's value) with the left label. The layout check also passes at 7 with the left label, but in Chromium the Anaconda bubble is then 6.8 px from Butte's at zoom 7 (rings included), so 8 was kept.
Belgrade's zoom is 9 (brief's value). The layout check passes at 8, but in Chromium the bubble sits 3.1 px from Bozeman's at zoom 8 (rings included) against 39.9 px at zoom 9, so 9 was kept.

Label widths: the three new names were measured in this Chromium (Anaconda 59.0, Belgrade 54.0, Sidney 41.0 px at 13 px bold). The 14 earlier widths differ from this browser by up to 1.6 px (Helena 42.4 vs 41; Bozeman 55.6 vs 54). They were left unchanged.

NWS live check: Anaconda's first point lookup returned HTTP 500, and the next requests returned 200. The build reuses the last good point lookup when one fails and says so when it has none, so a first build could show Anaconda without a forecast grid until a request succeeds. Offices: Belgrade TFX (Great Falls), Anaconda MSO (Missoula), Sidney GGW (Glasgow). All three are already in the build's OFFICES list, so no new office links were needed.

Left alone on purpose: AGENTS.md's label convention (it does not mention min_zoom; shared rules, not edited); docs/DESIGN.md line 188 ('14 cards' in a dated review table); the research/ notes; the DECISIONS D28 bullet on minor towns from zoom 7 (history). sample.py was not changed: every slug-keyed dict lookup already has a default, so the three new towns use those defaults in the sample.
build.notes:
Base map: website/static/map/basemap.json went from 384,594 to 384,935 bytes (+341; budget 450,000). The final build printed no builder notes. Against the committed file, the only label that moved is the phone-only "SK" (max_zoom 5), from 49.6917 to 49.725 N (about 0.03 degrees). Places went from 57 to 60: Anaconda (min_zoom 8), Belgrade (9) and Sidney (5) were added. No other label, place or layer changed. Several exploratory label-side variants printed notes, for example Glasgow right with Sidney left: "z5 Glasgow name / Sidney bubble 5.1 px", and Havre left: "z5 Havre name / Kalispell name".

Label sides: Anaconda left (right would put its name into Butte's bubble at zoom 7, 4.5 px; right also passes at 8). Sidney top (right would run across the Montana line into North Dakota; left hits Glasgow's bubble at zoom 5; bottom hits Miles City's name at zoom 5). Glasgow right to top (existing town; see open issues for the alternatives). Belgrade right (default, kept). Havre unchanged (left hits Kalispell's name at zoom 5; bottom hits Great Falls' name).

Measured in Chromium at 1280x800 and 390x844, zooms 5 to 11, rings included: no overlaps on desktop at any zoom. Tightest desktop pairs: Bozeman-Livingston bubbles 11.0 px apart at zoom 7; Anaconda-Butte 47.5 px at zoom 8; Belgrade-Bozeman 39.9 px at zoom 9. The same four-decimal coordinates were used for the NWS points.

Census: Wikipedia's list of Montana municipalities (fetched 2026-10-17) has 12 places over 8,000 in the 2020 column, and all 12 are now on the site. Confirmed: Anaconda 9,421, Belgrade 10,460, Sidney 6,346, Whitefish 7,751, Laurel 7,222. Lockwood and Evergreen are census-designated places per the brief.

Code changes beyond the brief, for review: map.css lost the two .town.minor rules. Towns now get "mzN" from zoomCls, the class that already hides basemap names below their zoom, and min_zoom 8 and 9 need it. map.js gained townMinZoom(t) (fallback: minor 7, else 5), which the four places call. The comment "the 14 site towns" became "the site towns". website/storm.py's docstring "14 towns" became "site towns". tools/smoke_map.py waits became state="attached". tests/test_site.py now derives the station IDs from the town order (Lewistown SMP111, Livingston SMP120 to SMP122) and uses len(site.TOWNS) in the observation-count string. New tests cover min_zoom in map.json, the tool's rule, the 5-to-9 range, and the map.js wiring. Docs: README (intro count, town table row, town list, towns.json row), DESIGN (two page counts and the min_zoom paragraph), ROADMAP (Town pages (17); open question answered), DECISIONS (D31 before the Gotchas section).

Read-only git commands only (status, diff, show, and an archive of HEAD into the scratch folder towns-base for the before-and-after build). Logs and scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/towns-work (baseline-check.log, build3.log, explore.py for variant runs, geometry.py, firstview.py, belgrade8.py, smoke-map-off.log, smoke-map-on.log, smoke-pages-off.log, unittest-final.log, screenshots in shots/). Sample sites: .../scratchpad/towns-off (default) and .../scratchpad/towns-on (--storm-layers). Downloaded sources are kept at .../scratchpad/basemap-src, so a rerun is fast. The committed-file copy from before the change is .../scratchpad/towns-work/basemap-before.json.

verify.tests: Branch check: claude/more-towns. Diff: git diff --stat = 14 files, 145 insertions, 45 deletions. Unit tests: python -m unittest discover -s tests = 281 tests OK (run before and after my one doc edit). Base map: python tools/build_basemap.py --src .../scratchpad/basemap-src --check = exit 0, committed file is up to date. Payload: python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload = PASS, payload 1.0.0. Sample builds: python -m website.build --out .../scratchpad/towns-verify-off --sample = exit 0; the same with --storm-layers (towns-verify-on) = exit 0. Browser smoke with PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium: tools/smoke_map.py on the off and on builds = Map smoke test passed (both); tools/smoke_pages.py on both = passed at 288, 320, 375, 768 and 1440 px, light and dark. Live build: python -m website.build --out .../scratchpad/towns-live --require-live = exit 0. Status: alerts ok (3 active); forecasts 17 of 17 towns; station readings 17 of 17 towns, all 17 under 75 minutes old; SPC reports ok (0 in 3 days); radar 7 frames; HRRR run 11:00 am MDT, 12 hours. New towns, live: Anaconda office MSO (Missoula), forecast issued 12:22 pm, station DRLM 16 mi away (gusts 28 mph, wind reported as not reported); Belgrade office TFX (Great Falls), forecast 12:31 pm, station KBZN 1 mi away (54 F, calm); Sidney office GGW (Glasgow), forecast issued 4:20 am, station KSDY 2 mi away (61 F, wind 14 mph S). Now page: 17 town cards. Town pages: all 17 open with HTTP 200 and their names in the title; anaconda, belgrade and sidney present. Browser checks (Chromium, live build, scratch script outside the repo): see notes. basemap.json: 384,594 to 384,935 bytes (+341), budget 450,000, test_under_budget passes.
failures: Step 5 read literally (no bubble may cover a name): at exactly zoom 5.00 on a phone (reached only by pinching out; the phone first view is 5.25), Miles City's name reaches 3.2 px into Sidney's bubble, bubble rings included. This is new from this change. It is inside the 4 px zoom-5 allowance that docs/DECISIONS.md documents, it is clear at zoom 5.25 and above, and main already has three name-into-bubble overlaps at zoom 5.00 (Missoula/Kalispell 4.5 px, Billings/Miles City 3.0 px, Havre/Glasgow 1.4 px). Not changed. See open_issues 1.
open_issues: 1. Miles City's name into Sidney's bubble at zoom 5.00 (3.2 px, new). Recommendation: accept, since it is inside the documented zoom-5 allowance and clear from zoom 5.25. Options tested in scratch copies (only data/map.json edited): Miles City's label on the right clears it at zooms 5.00, 5.25, 6 and 7 on a phone with no new overlap, but it changes an existing town's label. Sidney at min_zoom 6 also clears it, but Sidney is then hidden on phones below zoom 6, which the brief did not ask for. Sidney's own label side cannot fix it, because the overlap is with Sidney's bubble, which does not move.

2. Glasgow's label moved from right (the default) to top. This is the one towns.json change beyond the three additions, and it is needed to keep Sidney at min_zoom 5. With Glasgow's label on the right, its name reaches 7.0 px into Sidney's bubble at zoom 5.00 (measured in a scratch copy; the builder's report and D31 quote 5.1 px). With the label on top, Glasgow's name sits 1.1 px from Havre's name on phones at zoom 5.25 and 1.5 px at 5.00: not overlapping, but tight.

3. At 1280x800 the desktop map cannot go below zoom 6.5 (map.js fitMinZoom, the picture-fit rule), so Sidney at zoom 5 is only checkable on phones and narrow windows. Sidney was checked on the desktop at 6.5 (the minimum) and at 7.

4. Sample station IDs are SMP plus the town's index plus a station number, so adding towns renumbered the sample stations for Livingston (SMP100 to SMP120) and Lewistown (SMP091 to SMP111). tests/test_site.py now builds the expected IDs from site.TOWNS. It still asserts the exact card text, but it mirrors the sample formula instead of fixed IDs.

5. The distances in the brief do not match its coordinates, which are correct as given. Belgrade is 15.4 km NW of Bozeman (bearing 318 degrees), not 12 km west. Glendive is 79 km SSW of Sidney, not 65 km south. Anaconda is 34 km WNW of Butte, not 35 km. D31's gap figures match these coordinates when I recompute them: Belgrade to Bozeman bubbles about 3 px at zoom 8 and 39 px at zoom 9; Anaconda to Butte about 7 px at zoom 7 and 47 px at zoom 8.

6. Not verified: the live build with --storm-layers (only the sample with storm layers was built and smoke-tested); Anaconda's first NWS point lookup HTTP 500 that the builder's report describes (not reproduced; this run's lookup succeeded); real iPhone or Android devices (Chromium only, as ROADMAP says).
7. Side effect in basemap.json: the phone-only SK region label (zoom 5 only) moved about 0.03 degrees north, from 49.6917 to 49.725. The label test passes. I did not view it in a screenshot.

8. Anaconda's station DRLM reports gusts without a wind speed, so its town page shows the wind as not reported and gusts 28 mph. That is the station's data as displayed; I did not investigate it further.
9. Stale counts left on purpose: docs/DECISIONS.md lines 336 and 402 (dated 2026-10-16 entries) and docs/DESIGN.md line 190 (a dated review table).
verify.notes:
Edit made by me: docs/DESIGN.md only. One 143-character line in the minor-town paragraph is rewrapped into two lines; no words changed. Nothing committed or pushed, and no git state changed. git status shows the 14 modified files and no untracked files (only git-ignored __pycache__ folders from the test runs).

Read scope: each changed file's diff was read with its surrounding lines, which covers every changed line in map.js, build_basemap.py, build.py, storm.py, map.css, smoke_map.py, both test files, towns.json, the README, DESIGN, ROADMAP and DECISIONS entries, and the basemap.json diff. The unchanged parts of map.js, build_basemap.py and the test files were not re-read line by line; the unit tests and the browser checks cover them. basemap.json was checked as data (size, JSON validity through the build and the tests), not read.

Browser results (live build, Chromium, scratch script at .../scratchpad/towns-verify/browser_check.py): desktop 1280x800 reached zoom 7, 8 and 9 at Bozeman (7.00, 8.00, 9.00) and zoom 7 and 8 at Butte. Anaconda is hidden at 7 and shown at 8. Belgrade is hidden at 8 and shown at 9. Phones 390x844 and 360x740 reached zoom 5.00, 7, 8 and 9 at the requested towns, plus the 5.25 first view. In every view each town was drawn exactly when the zoom had reached its min_zoom. No page errors. Tapping Belgrade (zoom 9), Anaconda (zoom 8, desktop and phone) and Sidney (zoom 7 desktop, zoom 5 phone) opened its sheet with the right title. Real mouse input: a wheel gesture to zoom 9 at Belgrade, then a double-click to 9.5, both persisted for 2.5 s with Belgrade shown.

Overlaps, measured from the DOM with bubble rings included: desktop zoom 7 to 9: none. Closest pairs: Bozeman-Livingston bubbles 11.0 px at zoom 7 (on main too), Anaconda-Butte bubbles 47.5 px at zoom 8, Belgrade-Bozeman bubbles 39.9 px at zoom 9. Phone at 5.25 (first view) and 5.5: none. Closest at 5.25 are Glasgow and Havre names (1.1 px, new) and Billings and Miles City (2.1 px, on main too). Phone at 5.00: see failures. Main at 5.00, built from a git archive of HEAD (.../scratchpad/towns-verify/base-site), has the same contacts except the new Miles City/Sidney one and the Glasgow/Havre names 1.5 px apart: Missoula/Kalispell -4.5, Billings/Miles City -3.0, Havre/Glasgow -1.4, Bozeman/West Yellowstone bubbles 0.0, Kalispell name/Great Falls bubble 0.0.

Screenshots: .../scratchpad/towns-shots/ (70 PNG files: full views and 2x crops, plus report.json). I looked at seven by eye: phone first view, phone zoom 5.00 and 7 around Sidney, desktop first view, desktop Bozeman zoom 8, Belgrade zoom 9 and Anaconda zoom 8. All seven are legible, with no overlaps beyond the numbers above. The other views were checked by measurement only.

Census (Wikipedia list of municipalities, fetched 2026-10-17, saved in .../scratchpad/towns-verify/wiki): twelve municipalities over 8,000 in the 2020 column: Billings 117,116; Missoula 73,489; Great Falls 60,442; Bozeman 53,293; Butte 34,494; Helena 32,091; Kalispell 24,558; Belgrade 10,460; Anaconda 9,421; Havre 9,362; Miles City 8,354; Livingston 8,040. All twelve are on the site. Sidney is 6,346. Whitefish (7,751) and Laurel (7,222) are excluded. Lockwood and Evergreen are not in the table.

Method notes for future scripted tests: map.js counts only user gestures (wheel, arrow keys, drag, two-finger touch) as the viewer moving the map. A scripted setView needs a zero-delta wheel event first, or a banner or timeline change re-fits Montana. My first pass without that gave misleading zooms (6.75 for a requested 8); that was my harness, and the rerun above is the valid one. A variant copy with a wrong source path failed and was redone.

Variant copies (only data/map.json edited) are in .../scratchpad/towns-verify/variant-glasgow-right, variant-sidney-right, variant-milescity-right and variant-sidney-min6. They supply the option results in open_issues 1 and 2.

Logs: .../scratchpad/towns-verify-unittest.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify/unittest-final.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify-basemap-check.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify-build-off.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify-build-on.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify-smoke-map-off.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify-smoke-map-on.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify-smoke-pages-off.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify-smoke-pages-on.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify-live-build.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify/run2-new.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify/run2-base.log, .../scratchpad/towns-verify/selftest.log. Live site: .../scratchpad/towns-live.
